title: The Studio That Bought Its Rescuer
subtitle: Disney's own cartoons were failing, and its best partner was leaving. So in 2006 Disney bought Pixar — and asked Pixar to lead Disney's animation.

vocab.def: A person or company that works together with you.
vocab.ex: Pixar was Disney's partner for fifteen years.

vocab.def: A company that makes films, or the place where films are made.
vocab.ex: Pixar is a small studio in California.

vocab.def: Films made from drawings or computer pictures that seem to move.
vocab.ex: Toy Story was the first film made completely with computer animation.

vocab.def: An official written agreement between two people or companies.
vocab.ex: The contract said Disney owned the characters.

vocab.def: To speak angrily to someone because you do not agree.
vocab.ex: The two bosses argued about money.

vocab.def: A film, song or product that is very successful.
vocab.ex: Finding Nemo was a huge hit.

vocab.def: An agreement to buy, sell or work together.
vocab.ex: The deal cost Disney about 7.4 billion dollars.

vocab.def: The person who is in charge of a group or organisation.
vocab.ex: Pixar's leaders started to run Disney's animation too.

vocab.def: To keep someone or something safe.
vocab.ex: Disney promised to protect Pixar's way of working.

vocab.def: A film or book that continues the story of an earlier one.

vocab_discuss: What is your favourite animated film? Why do you like it?
Have you ever worked with a partner who was better than you at something? How did it feel?
Do you usually enjoy sequels, or is the first film always better?

story.heading: Part 1 — A small partner with big hits
paras: In 1986, Steve Jobs bought a small computer company for about ten million dollars. He called it Pixar.
For many years, Pixar lost money. But Jobs believed in it and kept paying.
In 1991 Pixar signed a contract with Disney. Pixar was going to make films, and Disney was going to sell them around the world.
In 1995 they released Toy Story. It was the first film made completely with computer animation. It earned more than 350 million dollars.
The next contract was good for Disney. Disney owned the films and the characters. It could also make sequels without Pixar.
Pixar made hit after hit: Toy Story 2, Monsters, Inc. and Finding Nemo.
But Disney's own animated films were not doing well. Some were very expensive and made little money.
Slowly, Disney needed its small partner more than its partner needed Disney.
tf: Pixar made money from its very first year.
Toy Story was the first film made completely by computer.
Under the contract, Pixar owned all its characters.
discuss: Why did Disney need Pixar more and more?
The contract was good for Disney. Was it fair for Pixar? Why or why not?

story.heading: Part 2 — The partners break up
paras: Steve Jobs and Disney's boss, Michael Eisner, did not get on. They argued about money and about who had control.
In January 2004 Pixar stopped the talks about a new contract. It was going to find a new partner after its last films with Disney.
Disney had a plan too. It was going to make Toy Story 3 without Pixar. It started a new team to do it.
Many Disney shareholders were angry with Eisner. Walt Disney's nephew, Roy Disney, started a campaign against him.
In 2004, about 43 per cent of shareholders' votes went against Eisner. He left the company in 2005.
The new boss was Bob Iger. Iger later wrote about a day at the new Disney park in Hong Kong.
He watched the parade. He saw that almost all the popular new characters were from Pixar, not from Disney's own studio.
tf: Jobs and Eisner had a very friendly relationship.
Disney planned to make Toy Story 3 without Pixar.
Bob Iger noticed something important while he watched a parade.
discuss: Disney was going to make Toy Story 3 without Pixar. Was that a good plan? Why or why not?
Iger learned something important from a parade, not from a report. Where do you get your best ideas?

story.heading: Part 3 — Who changed whom?
paras: In January 2006, Disney made a big deal. It bought Pixar for about 7.4 billion dollars.
Then Disney did something unusual. Pixar's leaders became the leaders of Disney's own animation studio too.
Pixar kept its name, its offices and its way of working. Disney promised to protect it. The team making Toy Story 3 without Pixar was closed.
It worked. Disney's own studio made Frozen in 2013. It earned about 1.3 billion dollars.
But the plan depended on a few people. In 2018 one Pixar leader left after complaints about his behaviour at work. The other leader retired in 2019.
In the 2020s, some Pixar films went straight to Disney's streaming service. One film did badly, and in 2024 Pixar cut jobs.
That same year, Inside Out 2 earned about 1.7 billion dollars, and Pixar planned more sequels.
So here is the question. Did Pixar change Disney? Or, slowly, did Disney change Pixar?
tf: After the deal, Pixar's leaders ran Disney's animation studio too.
Disney changed Pixar's name after it bought the company.
Frozen was made by Disney's own animation studio.
discuss: Why do you think Disney let Pixar's leaders run its own animation?
When a big company buys a small one, who usually changes? Give an example you know.
Tell the story again in six sentences. Use: was going to · were going to · wanted to · but.

grammar.name: was going to
grammar.heading: was / were going to — plans in the past
explain: In this story, people make plans — and then something different happens. English uses was / were going to for a plan in the past.
A plan that changed: I was going to study last night, but my friends came round.
Form: was (I, he, she, it) or were (you, we, they) + going to + verb.
Negative: We weren't going to buy anything, but the shoes were cheap.
Careful: after going to, use the verb with no -ing: was going to call (NOT calling).

practice.heading: Complete the sentences
practice.intro: Use was going to, were going to, Were, or the correct verb. Read the whole sentence first.
items: Pixar ___ find a new partner, but then Disney bought the company.
We ___ go to the beach, but it rained, so we stayed at home.
___ you going to come to the party? We waited for you!
They weren't going to ___ the house, but the price was very good, so they bought it.
My sister ___ be a doctor, but she became a teacher instead.

fix.heading: Find the mistake
items: I was going to calling you, but my phone died.
They was going to buy a new car.
She going to start a new job, but she changed her mind.
We were go to travel, but we stayed at home.
Was you going to tell me the news?
answers: I was going to call you, but my phone died. (no -ing after going to)
They were going to buy a new car. (they = were)
She was going to start a new job, but she changed her mind. (don't forget was)
We were going to travel, but we stayed at home. (not were go to)
Were you going to tell me the news? (you = were)

speak.label: 1 · Tell the story
paras: Tell me the story of Disney and Pixar in your own words. Six or seven sentences is enough.

speak.label: 2 · Plans that changed
paras: Tell me about three things you were going to do — this week, this year, or in your life — that you didn't do.
What happened instead?

speak.label: 3 · Working together
paras: Think of a time you worked with someone who was better than you at something.
Did you learn from them, or did you compete?

speak.label: 4 · Big and small
paras: Do you prefer shopping at big companies or small ones? Why?
What do small companies do better?

final: Is it better to buy a company that is beating you, or to try harder to beat it? Why?
When a big company buys a small one, what should it never change?
If you were Disney's boss in 2006, would you pay 7.4 billion dollars for Pixar? Why or why not?
